newsitem.title: UK: UK shares down in poll aftermath, utilities fall.
newsitem.headline: UK shares down in poll aftermath, utilities fall.

text.p: UK shares opened lower in jittery trading on Friday as the market recoiled at the bigger-than-expected election rout for the Conservative party, with Labour in government with a majority of about 180 seats.

Yet the early loss was less than some dealers had feared, with some arguing that the poll result should have been discounted and that the decisive poll outcome should ultimately prove positive for UK markets.
The FTSE 100 index of top stocks, which set a record close on the eve of the poll, was down just 14.6 points at 4,430.4 by 0752 GMT, defying overnight talk of an early 50-point tumble.

"There's an argument that we've known Labour was going to get in for months," said a dealer at one major securities house, "and now they've got such a huge majority there's a degree of certainty so we could see the market go higher."

Utility shares, in line for Labour's planned "windfall" tax, were among the biggest early losers and interest-rate sensitive banks also fell, though elsewhere declines were limited to a few pence at worst.
Even in water and electricity stocks, the decline was far from savage with United Utilities Plc for instance down just 14-1/2p at 654-1/2.
